title: PREVENT Risk Stratification for Intensive Blood Pressure Intervention and Life Expectancy in Rural China: A Post Hoc Analysis of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology guideline adopted the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations to guide antihypertensive treatment, but whether PREVENT risk groups identify patients who benefit more from intensive blood pressure (BP) control is uncertain. We evaluated intensive BP control across PREVENT risk groups in the China Rural Hypertension Control Project. METHODS: We analyzed 21 872 hypertensive adults from 326 Chinese villages. Participants received intensive BP control (target <130/80 mm Hg) or usual care and were classified as low risk (<5%), borderline risk (5.0%-7.4%), intermediate risk (7.5%-19.9%), or high risk (≥20%). The primary outcome was a composite of major cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Safety, net benefit, and life expectancy were assessed. RESULTS: Over a median of 3.02 years, intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the low-risk (hazard ratio, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.29-0.97]), intermediate-risk (hazard ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.49-0.69]), and high-risk groups (hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.47-0.77]), but not the borderline-risk group (hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.51-1.26]). No significant treatment-by-risk interaction was observed. Adverse events increased mainly in intermediate- and high-risk groups. Net benefit was favorable across all groups and greatest in the high-risk group. At 45 years of age, estimated life expectancy gains were 0.94 years overall, 0.71 years in the intermediate-risk group, and 1.26 years in the high-risk group. CONCLUSIONS: Intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in 3 PREVENT risk groups, with favorable net benefit across all groups. Absolute benefit and estimated life expectancy gains were greatest among high-risk participants. PREVENT risk stratification may inform intensive BP control in community-based hypertensive populations.

title: Association Between Peripheral and Coronary Subclinical Atherosclerosis Burden in Midlife
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals. METHODS: A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement. RESULTS: A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

title: Environmental noise and cardiometabolic health: a transatlantic perspective
abstract: Environmental noise is a pervasive but under-recognized cardiovascular and metabolic risk factor. Drawing on prior expert reviews and large-scale epidemiologic and mechanistic studies, this review synthesizes evidence on the burden, major clinical associations, biological pathways, vulnerable populations, and mitigation strategies relevant to cardiovascular health. Road traffic noise is consistently and dose-dependently associated with higher risks of ischaemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, diabetes, sleep disturbance, and adverse mental health outcomes, whereas for railway and aircraft noise, the evidence base is less consistent, although important associations are increasingly reported. Translational human imaging studies, controlled exposure experiments, and animal models converge on a common pathway in which chronic and intermittent noise exposure activates stress-responsive neural circuits, increases sympathetic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity, promotes oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular inflammation, and may thereby accelerate cardiometabolic disease. Noise frequently co-occurs with air pollution, heat, and adverse social and built environments, particularly in socioeconomically disadvantaged communities, and these combined exposures may contribute additively to cardiovascular risk. These effects are especially relevant in urban populations with nighttime exposure and multiple co-exposures. Despite this growing evidence base, environmental noise remains largely absent from contemporary cardiovascular risk assessment tools, prevention guidelines, and routine patient counselling, representing a missed opportunity for risk reduction. Effective mitigation will require a hierarchical strategy combining source reduction, health-informed urban and transport planning, and targeted individual protection. Reducing environmental noise exposure should be recognized as an important opportunity to protect and advance cardiovascular and metabolic health in the 21st century.

title: The Electrocardiogram as a Preventive Biomarker: From Conventional Risk Markers to Actionable Artificial Intelligence - A Narrative Review
abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an established tool in cardiovascular prevention, identifying silent arrhythmias, hypertrophy, prior myocardial infarction, conduction disease, and inherited electrical disorders. However, conventional interpretation captures only a fraction of the information embedded in the cardiac electrical signal. Because the ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, standardized, and already acquired at scale, it provides an attractive substrate for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening and risk stratification. Deep-learning models can identify latent signatures of ventricular dysfunction, structural heart disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and mortality risk. Importantly, evidence is beginning to extend beyond retrospective validation: prospective implementation studies have increased disease detection, while randomized data suggest that AI-ECG-guided clinical alerts may improve outcomes in selected high-risk populations. Whether such benefits extend to preventive populations remains uncertain. This review examines the preventive role of conventional, ambulatory, and wearable ECGs and distinguishes AI applications for detection, prediction, prognostication, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. We argue that performance metrics alone are insufficient. Preventive value requires a defined target population, calibrated and externally validated predictions, an appropriate confirmatory test, a feasible clinical workflow, and an intervention proven to improve outcomes. The most credible near-term applications are those that triage patients to established diagnostic pathways, such as echocardiography or prolonged rhythm monitoring. The central challenge is therefore to transform accurate AI-ECG predictions into actionable, affordable, scalable, safe, and equitable prevention.

title: Variable Interferences Dictate Different Cutoffs for Aldosterone Measured by Liaison and iSYS Chemiluminescence Immunoassays for the Seated Saline Suppression Test
abstract: BACKGROUND: Variable macromolecular-related interferences with different chemiluminescence immunoassays (CLIA) of plasma aldosterone, particularly at low concentrations during confirmatory tests, are a previously unrecognized problem. We therefore hypothesized that cutoffs for measurements of aldosterone for the seated saline suppression test require tailoring according to the particular immunoassay. METHODS: Multicenter study involving 609 patients with suspected primary aldosteronism who underwent seated saline suppression tests with aldosterone measured by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) compared with iSYS or Liaison CLIAs in 285 and 286 respective patients and a different LC-MS/MS method in 38 others. Cutoffs for plasma aldosterone were derived from receiver operating characteristic curves after classification of patients with (n=181) and without primary aldosteronism (n=336) by methods independent of confirmatory tests. For 92 patients classifications were not achieved. RESULTS: Youden's-index derived cutoffs for postsaline infusion plasma aldosterone were 300 and 272 pmol/L for measurements by respective Liaison and iSYS CLIAs compared with 169 pmol/L by LC-MS/MS. At those cutoffs, respective diagnostic sensitivities for Liaison and iSYS immunoassays and LC-MS/MS were 90% (CI, 84-97), 91% (CI, 86-97), and 98% (CI, 96-100) with specificities of 86% (CI, 80-91), 94% (CI, 80-91), and 90% (CI, 86-93). Improved disease confirmation according to specificities of 95% for measurements by Liaison and iSYS CLIAs and LC-MS/MS were provided by respective cutoffs of 436, 297, and 243 pmol/L but with reduced sensitivities of 64% (CI, 53-75), 85% (CI, 78-92), and 78% (CI, 72-84). CONCLUSIONS: Cutoffs for CLIA-based measurements of aldosterone during the seated saline suppression test are higher than those for LC-MS/MS and vary according to the specific immunoassay. Gray areas around cutoffs, particularly extensive for the Liaison CLIA, must also be considered. REGISTRATION: https://drks.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00017084.

title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age
abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking. METHODS: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68. RESULTS: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who received semaglutide and in 2% of those who received placebo. Adverse events occurred in 96% of the participants receiving semaglutide and in 93% of those receiving placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common, occurred more frequently with semaglutide than with placebo, and led to discontinuation in 1 participant in the semaglutide group. CONCLUSIONS: Among children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity, treatment with semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in a significantly greater mean percent reduction in BMI than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP Young ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05726227.).

title: Effectiveness of Bariatric Surgery and Incretin-based Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Obesity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies improve cardiometabolic risk factors. However, direct head-to-head comparisons assessing their impact on cardiovascular outcomes remain limited. We performed an exploratory meta-analysis to compare bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies on major clinical outcomes in adults with obesity. METHODS: A systematic literature search using PubMed and Scopus databases was conducted. Randomized and observational studies comparing bariatric surgery or incretin receptor agonists with controls were included in the analysis. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and MACE. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted across three nodes. RESULTS: A total of 40 studies, comprising more than 1.9 million patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with control, bariatric surgery was associated with a significant reduction in all evaluated outcomes, including all-cause mortality (HR:0.57, 95%CI:0.51-0.65), MACE (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.45-0.64), cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Incretin receptor agonists were also associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR:0.62, 95%CI:0.52-0.74), lower MACE (HR:0.75, 95%CI:0.61-0.92) and reduced heart failure hospitalization. All-cause mortality-representing the most direct and clinically relevant endpoint-did not differ significantly between the two strategies in the exploratory network meta-analysis. Importantly, the network estimates should be cautiously interpreted, given the predominance of observational evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and very low confidence across all comparisons. CONCLUSION: Bariatric surgery and incretin receptor agonists are associated with substantial reductions in major cardiovascular outcomes in adults with obesity. In head-to-head comparisons, no significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality and stroke. Both strategies provide clinically meaningful benefits.

title: Prognostic significance of incident microalbuminuria in a real-world population at increased cardiovascular risk: A report from a global federated research network
abstract: AIM: Despite growing interest in biomarker-based risk stratification for incident heart failure (HF), the prognostic value of newly detected microalbuminuria is poorly defined. This study evaluated its association with incident HF and cardiorenal outcomes in a large real-world cohort. METHODS: A total of 985,367 patients aged 40-80 years at increased cardiovascular (CV) risk but with no prior HF or chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage ≥3 was included from the TriNetX Global Research Network. Patients with persistent normoalbuminuria (UACR <30 mg/g) were compared to those with newly detected microalbuminuria (UACR 30-300 mg/g). The primary outcome was a composite of incident HF or all-cause mortality over a maximum 5-year follow-up. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: After matching, 150,250 patients were included in each group. Over a median follow-up of 2.5 [IQR range, 3.6] years, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite outcome (HR 1.29 [95% CI 1.25-1.34]), as well as higher incident HF (HR 1.31 [95% CI 1.26-1.36]), all-cause mortality (HR 1.43 [95% CI 1.35-1.51]), HFrEF (HR 1.61 [95% CI 1.51-1.71]), HFpEF (HR 1.37 [95% CI 1.29-1.45]), acute myocardial infarction (HR 1.33 [95% CI 1.25-1.41]), ischemic stroke (HR 1.27 [95% CI 1.20-1.35]) and increased risks of CKD progression to stage 3 (HR 2.80 [95% CI 2.67-2.93]) and stage 4 (HR 4.71 [95% CI 4.11-5.40]). In exploratory subgroup analyses, renal function showed the largest number of nominal interaction findings. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of patients at increased CV risk, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with higher cardiorenal risk, supporting further evaluation of UACR for early risk stratification.

title: Data-Driven Phenotyping of Stage 2 Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Among U.S. Adults
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stage 2 cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is common and represents an important window for primary prevention, but it encompasses heterogeneous cardiometabolic risk profiles. OBJECTIVES: We aim to identify the distinct phenotypes of stage 2 CKM among U.S. adults and characterize their temporal trends, sociodemographic distribution, and mortality risks. METHODS: We analyzed 8,761 adults aged ≥20 years with stage 2 CKM from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 1999 to 2018, with mortality follow-up through 2019. Latent profile analysis incorporated 9 age-residualized, standardized biomarkers across adiposity, blood pressure, glycemic, lipid, and kidney domains. We assessed the prevalence, trends, and sociodemographic distribution of the distinct stage 2 CKM phenotypes. Survey-weighted Cox models estimated mortality associations using CKM stages 0/1 as the reference. RESULTS: Four phenotypes were identified: lean-hypertensive (23.3%), overweight-dyslipidemic (40.7%), obesity-metabolic (26.2%), and hyperglycemic-albuminuric (9.8%). From 1999-2000 to 2017-2018, hyperglycemic-albuminuric increased from 6.0% to 12.1% and obesity-metabolic from 22.3% to 30.6%, whereas lean-hypertensive declined from 31.0% to 20.8% (all P for trend<0.001). Hyperglycemic-albuminuric was disproportionately prevalent among non-Hispanic Black adults and those with lower income or educational attainment. During a median 10-year follow-up, 484 deaths occurred, including 117 cardiovascular disease deaths. Hyperglycemic-albuminuric was associated with the highest risks of all-cause (HR: 2.59; 95% CI: 1.95-3.45) and cardiovascular disease mortality (HR: 4.49; 95% CI: 2.47-8.15). CONCLUSIONS: Stage 2 CKM comprises distinct phenotypes with differing cardiometabolic risk profiles, temporal trends, sociodemographic patterns, and mortality risk among U.S. adults. These findings underscore the need for targeted and equitable CKM prevention and management strategies.

title: Postoperative Inflammatory Response After Cardiac Surgery: Magnitude, Timing, and Prognosis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery triggers a systemic inflammatory response. While this response is commonly interpreted as a marker of postoperative complications, its prognostic significance on short- and long-term death remains poorly characterized. We assessed the association between postoperative inflammation and short- and long-term all-cause death after cardiac surgery. METHODS: In a single-center retrospective cohort of patients undergoing cardiac surgery between 2011 and 2024, postoperative CRP (C-reactive protein) measurements and peak of postoperative CRP (CRPmax) and its timing were assessed. Association between CRPmax tertiles, delayed CRPmax (after postoperative day 3), and 30-day or 5-year all-cause death were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression models. RESULTS: A total of 7283 patients were included (mean age, 64.9 years; 72% men; 54% underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, 31% aortic valve replacement, and 94% on-pump surgery). Median CRPmax was 184 interquartile range, 134-246) mg/L. Median postoperative CRP peaked on postoperative day 3. Patients in the highest CRPmax tertile (tertile 3) more frequently presented with obesity, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and chronic kidney disease. Compared with the lowest tertile, CRPmax tertile 3 was independently associated with higher 30-day (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.56 [95% CI, 1.78-3.68]; P<0.001) and 5-year all-cause death (adjusted HR, 1.41 [95% CI, 1.22-1.62]; P<0.001). A delayed CRPmax was independently associated with increased 30-day (adjusted HR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.94-3.52]; P<0.001) and 5-year mortality rate (adjusted HR, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.37-1.77]; P<0.001). These associations persisted after adjustment for postoperative infection. CONCLUSIONS: Both the magnitude and timing of postoperative CRP peak were independently associated with short- and long-term death after cardiac surgery, irrespective of postoperative infection. These findings support close postoperative inflammatory monitoring after cardiac surgery.

title: Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology
abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and incident peripheral artery disease in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an atherogenic, prothrombotic lipoprotein linked to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but prospective data on its association with peripheral artery disease (PAD) in large, diverse U.S. cohorts are limited. We characterized the association of Lp(a) with long-term incident PAD risk in a diverse, community-based U.S. METHODS: We included Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study participants attending Visit 4 (1996-98) with measured Lp(a) and no prevalent PAD. Lp(a) was natural logarithm (ln)-transformed and categorized as <30, 30-50, and >50 mg/dL. Incident PAD was identified from hospitalization and procedure codes through 2019. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models adjusted for confounders; Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions accounted for competing mortality. RESULTS: Among 9727 participants (mean age 63.1 years, 53.9% women, 20.4% Black), 825 incident PAD events occurred over a median 22.5 years of follow-up. Lp(a) was <30 mg/dL in 69.7%, 30-50 in 11.7%, and >50 in 18.6%. Fully adjusted HRs were 1.27 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-1.57) for 30-50 mg/dL and 1.32 (95% CI, 1.11-1.57) for >50 mg/dL versus <30 mg/dL; each unit increase in ln(Lp(a)) was associated with an HR of 1.14 (95% CI, 1.07-1.20). Estimates were similar accounting for competing mortality, and cumulative incidence differed across categories (p < 0.001). The association did not differ by baseline statin use. CONCLUSIONS: Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with greater long-term PAD risk in a community-based cohort, supporting Lp(a) as a risk factor for lower-extremity atherosclerotic disease and its value for risk stratification.

title: Association Between Saturated Fat Intake and Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Across the Genetic Spectrum
abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is a causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Guidelines recommend reducing saturated fat intake to lower LDL-C, but dietary effects are heterogeneous. OBJECTIVES: We examined whether genetic propensity for higher LDL-C modifies the association of saturated fat intake with LDL-C and incident ASCVD. METHODS: Among 20,940 genotyped Women's Health Initiative participants, we examined saturated fat intake from food frequency questionnaires and a polygenic score for LDL-C (PGSLDL). The primary outcome was LDL-C. The secondary outcome was incident ASCVD. Associations were assessed using multivariable linear and Cox regressions. Effect modification was evaluated using interaction terms and restricted cubic splines. Models included demographic, lifestyle, clinical, and genetic covariates. RESULTS: The association between saturated fat intake and LDL-C was modified by PGSLDL (P interaction for LDL-C = 0.01). Spline analysis revealed a nonlinear interaction, with increasing effect sizes across the upper end of the PGSLDL distribution. Among 16,835 participants without prevalent ASCVD, 1,582 experienced incident ASCVD (median follow-up: 10 years [Q1, Q3: 9.4, 10.0]). A 5% isocaloric increase in saturated fat intake was associated with a higher ASCVD risk among individuals in the top quartile of PGSLDL (HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.08-1.47), but no association was observed among those in the bottom 3 quartiles (HR: 1.00; 95% CI: 0.89-1.12); P interaction for ASCVD = 0.006. CONCLUSIONS: The association between saturated fat intake and LDL-C and subsequent ASCVD risk may be stronger for individuals with a genetic propensity towards high LDL-C.

title: Real-World Safety and Effectiveness of Evolocumab in Japanese Patients With Familial Hypercholesterolemia: Postmarketing Survey Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the real-world use of PCSK9 (proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9) inhibitors in familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) remains limited. This postmarketing surveillance study (NCT02808403) evaluated Japanese patients with FH and the long-term real-world effectiveness of evolocumab. METHODS: This analysis included patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) and homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH). Diagnostic pathways, patient characteristics, background lipid-lowering therapy, evolocumab use, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) reduction, long-term target achievement, and findings in pediatric HoFH were assessed. RESULTS: Of 2117 patients in the safety analysis set (HeFH, n=2009; HoFH, n=108), 1380 (HeFH, n=1296; HoFH, n=84) were included in the effectiveness analysis. Compared with patients with HeFH, patients with HoFH had higher genetic testing rates (40.7% versus 9.8%), higher mean baseline LDL-C levels (188.4±107.3 mg/dL versus 139.2±58.3 mg/dL), and higher lipoprotein apheresis use (26.9% versus 2.1%), but fewer total comorbidities (2.2±1.5 versus 2.7±1.5). Statin use was similarly high in patients with HeFH and HoFH (92.2% and 93.5%, respectively) with many patients receiving low- to moderate-intensity statins. Most patients received evolocumab biweekly. LDL-C reductions were evident at 4 weeks and sustained at 104 weeks. At 104 weeks, mean LDL-C changes from baseline were -54.0% in patients with HeFH and -48.9% in patients with HoFH. LDL-C<70 mg/dL was achieved by 63.0% of patients with HeFH and 43.9% of patients with HoFH, and LDL-C<55 mg/dL was achieved by 48.2% and 17.1%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Evolocumab was associated with sustained LDL-C reductions over 104 weeks in Japanese patients with HeFH and HoFH, with higher target achievement in HeFH. Gaps exist in genetic testing and treatment optimization in routine Japanese FH care.

title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research
abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes, characterised by spontaneous separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall. It predominantly affects younger women, and recent registry and imaging studies indicate that SCAD is more common than previously appreciated, challenging its historical classification as a rare condition. Clinically, SCAD is associated with a substantial early risk of adverse events, particularly in the first weeks after the index dissection. Given the high frequency of spontaneous healing, conservative management is preferred for most patients, whereas revascularisation is generally reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. However, evidence to guide both pharmacological and interventional management remains scarce. This Review summarises current evidence on SCAD epidemiology, underlying mechanisms including genetic susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, management principles, implications for reproductive and women's health, and research priorities to improve outcomes for affected patients.

title: Comparative Accuracy of the European Society of Cardiology Rapid Rule-Out and Rule-In Protocols for Diagnosing Non-ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Network Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: The European Society of Cardiology rapid rule-out and rule-in protocols using hs-cTns (high-sensitivity cardiac troponins) with blood collection at 0 and 1 hour (0/1 hour), 0 and 2 hours (0/2 hours), and 0 and 3 hours (0/3 hours) are accurate and widely used for evaluating non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction. This network meta-analysis aimed to identify the best performing hs-cTn assay. METHODS: We conducted database searches up to January 15, 2026, a dual screening and eligibility assessment, independent data extraction and risk of bias assessment, a network meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy, and assessment of the certainty of evidence. Only full-paired diagnostic accuracy studies conducted in the emergency department were included. RESULTS: Ten prospective studies (15 publications) comparing 10 assays using the 0-/1-hour algorithm (n=8769), 0-/2-hour algorithm (n=1881), and 0-/3-hour algorithm (n=1236) were included. Comparisons between newer and conventional assays largely stemmed from a single-source study. Across all assays, the European Society of Cardiology 0-/1-hour algorithm demonstrated high sensitivity (summary point estimate range: 97.8%-99.8%). Furthermore, it maintained high specificity (89.8%-98.1%), with no assay showing clear superiority. The summary sensitivity and specificity did not show significant differences across assays after adjusting for biases because of imperfect reference standards. Comparative data in the European Society of Cardiology 0-/2-hour and 0-/3-hour algorithms were limited. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence remains insufficient to establish the superiority of any specific hs-cTn assay within the European Society of Cardiology 0-/1-hour algorithm. Although practical considerations may currently guide selection, continued validation of newer assays remains necessary.

title: Sex-specific mortality in ischaemic heart disease across Western Europe: 2023 Global Burden of Disease
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Ischaemic heart disease (IHD) mortality has declined across Western Europe, but conventional mortality rates may obscure whether women and men experience comparable outcomes once IHD is present. This study examined sex-specific prevalence-adjusted IHD mortality and risk factor-attributable population case fatality across Western European countries. METHODS: Global Burden of Disease 2023 estimates for IHD mortality and prevalence across Western European countries from 2013 to 2023 were analysed. Population case fatality was calculated as age-standardized mortality divided by age-standardized prevalence (mortality-to-prevalence ratio [MPR]). Risk factor-attributable mortality was normalized to IHD prevalence to derive case-fatality indices (CFIs) for metabolic, behavioural, dietary, and environmental exposures. Sex differences were quantified using women-to-men ratios (WMRs). Substantive disparities were defined by WMR deviation ≥20% from unity with <50% overlap of sex-specific uncertainty intervals. RESULTS: Between 2013 and 2023, IHD age-standardized mortality declined by 15.9% in men and 23.5% in women. The pooled Western Europe MPR decreased, from 2.26% to 2.09% in men and from 2.56% to 2.21% in women. Despite these improvements, substantive female excess in MPR was observed in Austria, France, Greece, Israel, Italy, and Spain, whereas substantive male excess was observed only in Iceland. Risk-specific CFIs showed female excess mainly for metabolic risk, low physical activity, and low fibre intake, whereas male excess was most evident for smoking and sugar-sweetened beverages. CONCLUSIONS: Declining IHD mortality across Western Europe conceals persistent sex-specific differences in population case fatality. Sex-disaggregated MPR and risk-specific CFIs may complement conventional surveillance and identify ecological signals, where declining mortality appears disproportionate to the estimated IHD burden.

title: Impact of age on implementation and tolerability of guideline-directed medical therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Elderly patients constitute a growing proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. We evaluated the impact of age on the implementation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in HFrEF. METHODS: TITRATE-HF is a prospective, multicentre registry (enrolment June 2022-February 2024) including patients with de novo, chronic, and worsening heart failure (HF). For the current analysis, HFrEF patients were categorized by age (<65, 65-74, and ≥75 years). We assessed GDMT implementation, tolerability, and clinical outcomes (composite endpoint: first HF hospitalization or all-cause death). RESULTS: The cohort included 980 patients aged <65 years (29%), 1120 patients aged 65-74 years (33%), and 1267 patients aged ≥75 years (38%). At 12-month follow-up, younger patients more frequently received GDMT, with quadruple therapy prescribed in 68% of those aged <65 years, 61% aged 65-74 years, and 51% aged ≥75 years (P < .001). In de novo HFrEF, age-related differences were observed within weeks after diagnosis, with faster and more extensive GDMT intensification in younger patients. Still, rates of treatment downgrades and the distribution of side effects were largely similar across age groups. Significant left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement was observed in all age groups (all P < .001). The use of quadruple therapy at 6 months was associated with a lower risk of the composite endpoint between 6 and 12 months (adjusted hazard ratio 0.65, 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.86, P = .002), with consistent associations across age groups (P for interaction = .46). CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients with HFrEF received less intensive GDMT. Age-related differences emerged early after diagnosis, with fewer treatment intensifications in elderly patients but largely similar downgrade rates across age groups. These findings highlight the need for improved implementation strategies to optimize guideline-directed therapy and dosing levels in the ageing HFrEF population.

title: Anemia and Iron Status in Pregnant and Postpartum Women With Acute Heart Failure
abstract: IMPORTANCE: In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), iron-deficient anemia is highly prevalent and may compound the cardiovascular stress of pregnancy, yet its contribution to maternal acute heart failure (AHF) is poorly understood. OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association of maternal anemia and iron status with AHF in pregnancy and post partum in India. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, unmatched, prospective case-control study recruited participants from 10 hospitals across 4 Indian states from February 2019 to November 2024. Incident cases were pregnant or postpartum women with clinically diagnosed AHF. Controls were women without history or symptoms of heart disease within 48 hours post partum. Data were analyzed from March 2025 to April 2026. EXPOSURES: Maternal anemia and iron status. Blood samples collected at recruitment were analyzed for hemoglobin, ferritin, transferrin saturation, soluble transferrin receptor, and hepcidin. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The outcome of interest was AHF, defined using clinical criteria. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations of iron status and anemia with AHF, adjusting for potential confounders, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Subgroup analyses were performed in women with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. The discriminatory capacity of a model including anemia present before AFH onset vs a model with established risk factors only was examined using receiver operating characteristic curves. RESULTS: Among 532 women with clinically diagnosed AHF (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-29] years) and 1091 controls (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-28] years), moderate and severe anemia were associated with 1.5-fold (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.52; 95% CI, 1.13-2.05) and 5-fold (aOR, 5.06; 95% CI, 3.02-8.48) increased odds of AHF, respectively, compared with women without anemia. Higher soluble transferrin receptor levels (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.31-1.57) and the lowest hepcidin quintile (aOR, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.69-4.14), both indicative of iron deficiency, were independently associated with AHF. These associations persisted after adjusting for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and after excluding women with preexisting cardiac conditions, and they were consistent in subgroups with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. Adding anemia to established risk factors improved model discrimination for identifying AHF risk, increasing the AUC from 78% (95% CI, 76%-81%) to 83% (95% CI, 80%-85%) (P < .001). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: This case-control study found that maternal anemia and iron deficiency were independently associated with AHF during pregnancy and post partum. Further studies are needed to determine whether preventing or treating iron deficiency and anemia can reduce AHF risk and improve maternal outcomes.

title: Early Implementation of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock Supported by Micro-Axial Flow Pumps
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) supported by mechanical circulatory support remains poorly defined. The feasibility and potential benefits of early GDMT initiation during Impella support are uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed a multicenter prospective registry of consecutive patients with CS treated with Impella between 2020 and 2024. GDMT exposure was defined as the number of heart failure therapies administered at device explantation. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinical severity and early shock trajectory. Landmark analysis excluded patients dying within 5 days, while mixed-effects models accounted for center-level clustering. RESULTS: Among 140 patients (mean age 61 years; 20% female), 40% received concomitant ECMO (ECPella). In-hospital mortality was 38%. At explantation, 43% received at least one GDMT agent. Greater GDMT exposure was independently associated with lower mortality (OR 0.28 per additional therapy; 95% CI 0.14-0.58; p<0.001). This association remained consistent in landmark analysis (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.16-0.66; p<0.001) and after excluding patients with cardiac arrest (adjusted OR 0.48; 95% CI 0.23-0.88; p=0.002). A graded relationship between GDMT intensity and survival was observed. Center-level variability was negligible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

title: Pulmonary Artery Pressures Predict Heart Failure Events Following Heart Failure and Non-Heart Failure Events
abstract: BACKGROUND: It is uncertain whether pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) within the first week after either hospitalization for a non-heart failure event (HFE) or hospitalization or urgent visit for a HFE predicts the risk of recurring events. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to determine if PAP following a non-HFE or HFE predicts subsequent events within 90 days. METHODS: The authors examined non-HFE and HFE in patients with heart failure (HF) treated with remote hemodynamic-guided management using a wireless PAP sensor in the GUIDE-HF study. They compared PAP trends before and after a non-HFE or HFE and stratified the admitting and discharge PAP during the index event into groups with a subsequent HFE, non-HFE, or no further events within 90 days. RESULTS: Following index non-HFE (615 events, n = 425), post-discharge diastolic PAP was significantly higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.3 ± 7.9 mm Hg) (n = 97) vs patients with a subsequent non-HFE (20.4 ± 7.3 mm Hg; P = 0.0046) (n = 189) or no further events (20.9 ± 7.4 mm Hg; P = 0.015) (n = 329). Following index HFE (539 events, n = 358), post-discharge diastolic PAP was numerically higher in patients with a subsequent HFE (23.9 ± 6.9 mm Hg) (n = 199) than in patients with a subsequent non-HFE (22.0 ± 7.1 mm Hg; P = 0.078 (n = 102) and in those with no further events (22.0 ± 7.6 mm Hg; P = 0.021) (n = 238). Similar trends were observed for HF with reduced ejection fraction and HF with preserved ejection fraction subgroups and with systolic and mean PAP. CONCLUSIONS: Persistently elevated PAP early after discharge following either an index non-HFE or an HFE is associated with the risk of a subsequent HFE. (Hemodynamic-GUIDEd Management of Heart Failure [GUIDE-HF]; NCT03387813).

title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of heart failure patients referred to cardiac rehabilitation: SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry
abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To assess the referral rate to cardiac rehabilitation (CR), the clinical profile of referred vs nonreferred patients, and the association between referral and clinical events in Spanish heart failure (HF) units. METHODS: The SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort of patients with HF in units accredited by the Spanish Society of Cardiology. Patients were classified according to CR referral and were followed up for up to 400 days for all-cause death, HF hospitalization or decompensation, and the combined endpoint of death or HF hospitalization, with outcomes analyzed using Cox regression. RESULTS: Of 2236 patients, 219 (9.8%) were referred to CR. Referred patients were younger (65.2  ±  11.7 vs 71.7  ±  12.2 years), more often male (73.5% vs 63.2%) and more frequently had an ischemic etiology (50.5% vs 28.8%), fewer comorbidities and more frequent use of quadruple therapy (59.4% vs 46.0%); 74.4% had HF with reduced ejection fraction (11.9% had HF with preserved ejection fraction, and 13.7% HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction). The lower crude rate of the combined endpoint (HR, 0.75; 95%CI, 0.56-1.01) was no longer observed after adjustment (HR, 0.99; 95%CI, 0.71-1.38), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: CR referral was infrequent and preferentially directed toward younger patients with ischemic HF with reduced ejection fraction, a lower comorbidity burden, and optimized therapy, whereas older patients, patients with multimorbidity, and those with HF with preserved ejection fraction remained underrepresented. The lower crude event rate was no longer observed after adjustment for measured baseline characteristics, and the observational design does not allow conclusions on the effect of CR itself.

title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM. METHODS: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function. RESULTS: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death. CONCLUSIONS: Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05648825.

title: Implementation Feasibility and Clinical Utility of Phenomapping in Dilated and Hypokinetic Non-dilated Non-ischemic Cardiomyopathy
abstract: AIMS: Despite phenotypic heterogeneity, the management of idiopathic non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains generalized and dominantly guided by left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF) and NYHA class. We aimed to develop a point-of-service phenomapping pathway for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy (HNDC) at time of CMR imaging leveraging the integration of i) patient self-reported health status, ii) imaging phenotype, and the iii) electronic health record (EHR). METHODS AND RESULTS: 1,355 patients (752 DCM and 603 HNDC) were followed for the composite MACE outcome of mortality, heart failure hospitalization or ventricular arrhythmia. K-means clustering was independently applied to DCM and HNDC derivation cohorts using 55 routinely captured features (16 patient-reported health variables, 19 CMR-derived, 14 EHR-derived, and 6 combined features), identifying three phenogroups in each cohort. Over a median of 3.9 and 3.7 years, 145 DCM patients (22%) and 65 HNDC patients (13%), respectively, experienced MACE. Adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and LV EF, phenogroup membership was independently associated with future outcomes. In DCM, the adjusted HR (95% CI) of phenogroups 2 and 3 versus Phenogroup 1 were 2.8 (1.6-4.8) and 3.5 (1.9-6.5), respectively (p<0.001 for both). In HNDC, Phenogroup 3 demonstrated an adjusted HR of 4.2 (1.7-10.2; p=0.001) versus Phenogroup 1. Prospective phenogroup assignment was enabled by a decision tree-classifier and validated in a temporal hold-out cohort. CONCLUSION: Phenomapping delivers incremental value to LVEF and NYHA for identification of high-risk NICM patients. These findings support value from standardized, point-of-service data integration for the delivery of phenomics-driven personalized care.

title: Identifying Plasma Proteins for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Penetrance and Severity in Pathogenic Variant Carriers and Noncarriers
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a clinically variable disease in onset and progression. Pathogenic MYBPC3 variants account for a substantial proportion of HCM diagnoses. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to identify protein biomarkers associated with HCM penetrance and severity. METHODS: Olink-assayed plasma proteins of 144 pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers were evaluated for associations with HCM severity based on diagnostic criteria (unaffected, mildly, or severely affected). Identified proteins were replicated in the UK Biobank considering time to onset of HCM (67 cases), cardiomyopathy (156 cases), and associations with left ventricular maximum wall thickness (6,492 participants). After prioritizing proteins on cardiac tissue expression and druggability, we examined disease penetrance through associations with heart failure (HF) and arrhythmic outcomes in 272 UK Biobank participants with known pathogenic HCM variants free of cardiomyopathy at proteomics assessment. RESULTS: Among pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers, we identified 27 proteins associated with HCM severity, of which 22 replicated in the UK Biobank. Six proteins were prioritized (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP], growth/differentiation factor [GDF]-15, fibroblast growth factor [FGF]-23, adrenomedullin [ADM], renin [REN], and neural cell adhesion molecule 1 [NCAM1]), of which 5 associated with disease penetrance in pathogenic variant carriers: NT-proBNP and REN associated with increased HF and arrhythmic risk, GDF-15 and FGF-23 with HF risk, and NCAM1 with arrhythmic risk. CONCLUSIONS: Through the integration of proteomic analyses in both clinical and general population cohorts, we replicated and prioritized 6 proteins associated with HCM penetrance and severity. These findings highlight potential plasma-based markers for diagnosis and disease monitoring, as well as promising targets for future therapeutic development.

title: Sex-Specific Phenotypic Architecture in Cardiac Amyloidosis Identified by Explainable Machine Learning
abstract: BACKGROUND: Females are under-represented in cardiac amyloidosis (CA), but whether this reflects sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity or differences in disease prevalence remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to characterize sex-associated differences in presentation and prognosis across CA subtypes using unsupervised clustering. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 2,216 patients with confirmed CA enrolled between 2010 and 2022: light-chain amyloidosis (AL) (n = 583), variant transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) (n = 432), and wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRwt) (n = 1,201). Self-organizing maps with k-means partitioning were applied separately to each subtype, and conditional inference trees identified key phenotypic discriminators. RESULTS: Females represented 40.8%, 33.8%, and 15.9% of AL, ATTRv, and ATTRwt cohorts, respectively. Clustering identified 4 AL, 6 ATTRv, and 6 ATTRwt phenotypes. Across subtypes, female-predominant clusters generally showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, lower cardiac remodeling burden, and less pronounced biomarker elevation. Female-predominant AL clusters included preserved-function and multisystem profiles, whereas ATTRv clusters included neurologic-dominant and older cardiometabolic profiles. In ATTRwt, females were predominantly represented in a phenotype characterized by preserved systolic function and less structural remodeling. Conditional inference trees identified sex as the first discriminator in ATTRwt and a secondary discriminator in AL, whereas ATTRv clusters were primarily discriminated by cardiac variables and sex was not selected. CONCLUSIONS: Unsupervised clustering identified female-predominant phenotypes with less structural cardiac remodeling but distinct multisystem characteristics across CA subtypes. These findings support sex-associated phenotypic heterogeneity in CA and generate hypotheses regarding female underrepresentation in contemporary CA cohorts.

title: Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation: From Prolapse to Precision Therapy
abstract: Degenerative mitral valve regurgitation due to mitral valve prolapse affects ≈15 million people globally and is the commonest indication for mitral intervention in high-income countries, but its biology, natural history, and lifetime management are ill defined. This review summarizes current knowledge of the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, and lifetime management of degenerative mitral regurgitation, with a focus on areas of uncertainty, recent advances, and emerging research directions. These include translational research focused on determining genetic and cellular drivers of disease progression and mechanistic studies geared to improve detection and prevention of downstream myocardial dysfunction, particularly in high-risk phenotypes, including arrhythmic mitral prolapse. The current landscape of randomized trials and large registries comparing contemporary surgical and transcatheter treatment and strategies to improve patient access to care and outcomes across all patient risk profiles and populations are also discussed.

title: Aortic Valve Stenosis Screening Using Deep Learning on Noninvasive Arterial Pressure Waveforms
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic stenosis (AS) presents a significant health burden. Early identification of significant AS, defined as at least moderate AS, may facilitate timely confirmatory testing, referral, and management. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop and externally validate a deep learning model applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a noninvasive finger-cuff system to screen for significant AS, using transthoracic echocardiography as the reference standard. METHODS: This prospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted from December 2020 through July 2025. Participants underwent concurrent transthoracic echocardiography and noninvasive arterial pressure waveform acquisition. A 1-dimensional convolutional neural network was developed using the Cleveland Clinic development cohort and evaluated in a temporally distinct, multicenter validation cohort including sites in the United States, Spain, and the Netherlands. RESULTS: Significant AS was present in 307 of 3,634 (8.4%) patients in the development cohort and 241 of 1,336 (18.0%) in the validation cohort. In the validation cohort, the model demonstrated an area under the curve of 0.893 (95% CI: 0.876-0.910), with a sensitivity of 92.5% (223/241; 95% CI: 88.5%-95.2%), negative predictive value of 97.5% (706/724; 95% CI: 96.1%-98.4%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 36.4% (223/612; 95% CI: 32.7%-40.3%). For severe AS, the area under the curve was 0.906 (95% CI: 0.890-0.922), with a sensitivity of 94.3% (183/194; 95% CI: 90.1%-96.8%), negative predictive value of 98.5% (706/717; 95% CI: 97.3%-99.1%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 32% (183/572; 95% CI: 28.3%-35.9%). CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a finger-cuff system serves as a promising screening test for significant AS.

title: Sex-Related Differences in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Primary Mitral Regurgitation: PRIME-MR Registry Insights
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences have been previously explored in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) undergoing surgery as well as those with secondary MR treated with transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate sex-related differences in baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TEER for primary MR. METHODS: Outcomes of Patients Treated with M-TEER for Primary MR (NCT05332782) is an international, retrospective registry including patients undergoing TEER for primary MR in 27 centers. The primary outcome was a composite of 2-year all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: A total of 2,078 patients, including 961 (46.3%) females, were analyzed. Females were older and had fewer comorbidities but presented with a different anatomy and more advanced symptoms. Compared with males, females were more frequently excluded from surgery because of advanced age and frailty. Optimal procedural results were lower in females, with a higher incidence of residual MR ≥2+ (38.5% vs 32.1%; P = 0.0037), and a significantly higher mean transmitral gradient (4.0 vs 3.6 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality in female patients. In contrast, the incidence of the primary composite endpoint, as well as heart failure hospitalization alone, did not differ significantly. After adjusting for comorbidities, females demonstrated lower primary composite endpoint (HR: 0.77; P = 0.009), lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.62; P < 0.001), and lower cardiovascular mortality (subdistribution HR: 0.53; P = 0.011). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with primary MR, females were older and presented with a different clinical and anatomical profile compared with males. Although optimal procedural results were lower in females, higher survival rates in females vs males suggest that mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be a good option regardless of sex.

title: Three-year outcomes of balloon-expandable valve-in-valve aortic valve implantation for failed transcatheter versus surgical valves
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve (TAV)-in-TAV compared with TAV-in-surgical aortic valve (SAV) implantation for failed bioprosthetic valves have been limited to short-term outcomes. AIMS: This study compared midterm outcomes between patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and those undergoing TAV-in-SAV. METHODS: From June 2015 to June 2024, 543 consecutive patients undergoing valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) were identified at our centre. After exclusion of ineligible patients, 109 patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and 349 undergoing TAV-in-SAV were included. Following propensity score matching, 214 patients (107 per group) were analysed. RESULTS: Three-year all-cause mortality did not differ between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups (hazard ratio 1.06, 95% confidence interval: 0.56-1.98; p=0.867). Similarly, no significant differences were detected in secondary outcomes. Over 3 years, the aortic valve mean pressure gradient was consistently lower and the aortic valve area was consistently larger in the TAV-in-TAV group compared with the TAV-in-SAV group. Concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary obstruction were more frequent in the TAV-in-SAV group than in the TAV-in-TAV group (22.4% vs 8.4%; p=0.006; 10.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.018, respectively). Post-ViV-TAVI computed tomography analysis showed that the waist level was the least expanded segment in both groups. However, expansion at this level was significantly greater in the TAV-in-TAV group than in the TAV-in-SAV group. CONCLUSIONS: There was no significant difference in 3-year mortality between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups. However, TAV-in-SAV was associated with higher rates of concomitant PCI and coronary obstruction, as well as lower valve expansion.

title: Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

title: Fully Automated, Explainable AI Analysis of Coronary CTA Improves Prediction of Major Cardiovascular Events
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is central to noninvasive diagnosis and risk assessment, yet current workflows are labor-intensive and depend on semiquantitative scoring systems that do not fully leverage prognostic information in CCTA. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study were to develop and validate a fully automated, explainable artificial intelligence (AI) system (AI-automated coronary analysis [ACA]) for comprehensive CCTA analysis to predict major adverse cardiovascular events and compare its performance with conventional risk markers. METHODS: AI-ACA automatically extracts a suite of CCTA-derived biomarkers, including stenosis severity, plaque burden, and composition; AI-derived CAD - reporting and data system (CAD-RADS) (AI-CADRADS); coronary tortuosity; and subtended myocardial mass, to generate interpretable risk estimates. In a retrospective cohort (n = 1,702), we compared AI-ACA with Agatston score, standard demographic risk markers, and AI-CADRADS. Model explainability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations. RESULTS: AI-ACA demonstrated higher predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.81) than Agatston score (AUC: 0.76) and demographic markers (AUC: 0.67), and similar performance to AI-CADRADS (AUC: 0.81). AI-ACA showed better prognostic discrimination than Agatston score, reflected by a higher Harrell C-index (0.791 vs 0.742) and greater separation in event-free survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank 31.79 vs 13.71). Shapley Additive Explanations analysis identified total plaque volume and burden, maximum stenosis severity, and AI-CADRADS as the strongest contributors to risk estimation. CONCLUSIONS: A fully automated and explainable AI platform for CCTA enables comprehensive quantitative characterization of CAD without manual intervention. Although prognostic performance was comparable to AI-CADRADS and modestly higher than Agatston score, the platform provides transparent biomarker-based risk assessment and scalable analysis that may facilitate broader clinical implementation of quantitative CCTA.

title: Multiview Integration for Robust Echocardiographic Embeddings: Accessible AI for Clinical Practice
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although recent artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models have shown superior performance in medical imaging, their high computational demands and reliance on large data sets limit accessibility. These issues are especially pronounced in echocardiography, where integrating complex multiview measurements for individual cases hinders AI development and clinical translation. Vector embedding approaches offer promising solutions by leveraging compact representations in AI applications. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to develop a transformer-based multiview encoder that integrates multiple echocardiographic videos into unified vector embeddings and uses adversarial learning to reduce reliance on demographic shortcuts. METHODS: Using the MIMIC-IV-ECHO (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV-Echocardiography) data set (7,169 studies), we trained a multiview encoder to produce study-level embeddings and evaluated them on 21 binary classification tasks covering echocardiographic measurements and clinical diagnoses. We varied adversarial weights to assess their impact on demographic shortcut reliance and overall performance. RESULTS: The multiview encoder raised the mean area under the curve (AUC) across clinical tasks from 0.742 to 0.831 compared with the foundation model embedding (ΔAUC +0.090; 95% CI: 0.078-0.100), with significant gains in 20 of 21 tasks. The embeddings remained robust with a limited number of views (mean ΔAUC +0.071; 95% CI: 0.043-0.113). Adversarial learning reduced sex and race predictability only at strong weights and at substantial cost to clinical performance. CONCLUSIONS: The multiview encoder framework integrates multiple echocardiographic views into unified study-level embeddings, enabling substantial diagnostic improvements across diverse cardiac tasks. By producing compact, informative embeddings without requiring extensive computational resources, this approach lowers the cost of building echocardiographic AI on an existing foundation model.

title: Systematic Transesophageal Echocardiographic Identification of Tricuspid Valve Commissures and Subvalvular Apparatus
abstract: Transcatheter tricuspid valve (TV) intervention is rapidly evolving and several classes of therapeutic devices are currently in development. The anatomic knowledge of the TV is the cornerstone for transcatheter patient selection, and the successful implantation of the devices depends on imaging guidance. Anatomically, leaflets are separated by the commissures, which have peculiar findings: they are supported by fan-shaped chords and do not open directly into the annulus, but a few millimeters of the leaflet tissue remain, similar to small scallops. While a comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of TV has been extensively reported, few papers have focused on analyzing commissures and their impact on interventions. This paper aims to introduce a novel echocardiographic approach focusing on TV commissures, and provide a dedicated transesophageal imaging protocol and methodology for recognizing their anatomic landmarks. Multiple dedicated transesophageal views are comprehensively reported for each commissure, in order to ensure a guide for emerging transcatheter procedures.

title: Heart Failure Phenotyping and Prognosis by CMR-Derived Oxygen Delivery and Extraction
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure reflects impaired matching of systemic oxygen delivery to metabolic demand, yet resting oxygen transport is seldom measured. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to noninvasively derive resting oxygen delivery and extraction using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and relate these to clinical characteristics and outcomes. METHODS: In this retrospective study, in patients with heart failure referred for clinical CMR, cardiac output was assessed by cine imaging; basal blood-pool T2 mapping provided imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation; and measured hemoglobin enabled calculation of arterial oxygen content. Arterial oxygen saturation was fixed at 96%. We derived indexed systemic oxygen delivery (DO2i), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), and indexed systemic oxygen consumption (VO2i). The endpoint was all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: A total of 429 patients were included (62 events). VO2i varied widely (tertile means 138.8, 207.9, and 293.8 mL/min/m2), while left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (38.8%, 40.6%, and 40.3%; P = 0.42). Imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation decreased across increasing VO2i tertiles (61.5%, 54.3%, and 50.7%; P < 0.0001). In Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, ejection fraction, and late gadolinium enhancement, VO2i was associated with the endpoint (HR: 1.15 per 50 mL/min/m2, 95% CI: 1.00-1.32; P = 0.046), but discrimination of VO2i alone was poor (Harrell's C = 0.53). Delivery-extraction phenotypes differed in event risk (log-rank P = 0.026): event proportions were 8.6% (high DO2i/low OEF), 14.0% (low DO2i/low OEF), 16.8% (high DO2i/high OEF), and 18.3% (low DO2i/high OEF). The delivery-extraction phenotype remained associated with outcome after adjustment for age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction, and CMR-derived filling pressure. CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating study, CMR-based oxygen supply-demand assessment delineates resting delivery-extraction phenotypes associated with heart failure outcomes.

title: Precise anatomical landmark annotation of the cardiac conduction system on cardiac computed tomography angiography
abstract: BACKGROUND: CTA-based estimation of the conduction system from anatomical landmarks underpins a visualization platform (CARA) used in structural heart interventions and conduction system pacing. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the precision and reliability of the annotation method and the bias of trained readers relative to an expert reference standard. METHODS: The expert who defined the method and 6 trained readers each annotated 8 landmarks representing the sinus and atrioventricular nodes, His bundle course (Point B), left bundle branch origin (Point C), and course of Bachmann's bundle (B2-B5), in addition to the three aortic leaflet nadirs on 50 CTA studies in 3 sessions. Repeatability and reproducibility were assessed, referenced to clinically accepted error margins (2-5 mm). Intraclass correlations (ICC) were computed on heights above the aortic annular plane. 3D bias relative to the expert was tested for equivalence within half the margin. RESULTS: Repeatability SD was 1.67-3.98 mm and reproducibility SD 2.03-5.60 mm; all mean deviations were within margin, with 88.6-97.4% of repeat reads and 71.4-94.9% of reader means within margin. Inter-observer ICC on annular heights was 0.76-0.82 for the atrioventricular and 0.79-0.98 for the atrial points. Shared bias relative to the expert was 0.14-3.24 mm, within margin for all landmarks and equivalent within half the margin for sinus node, Point B, B2 and B3; at B3 and B2, 95% and 83% of the apparent separation was repeatability noise. CONCLUSION: The method meets its clinically accepted margins with millimeter precision and good-to-excellent reliability, and transfers from expert to trained readers with bias within margin.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Super-High-Pressure Noncompliant Balloons for Treatment of Calcified Coronary Lesions: The VICTORY Trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although calcified coronary lesions are associated with poor outcomes after percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI), randomized data guiding lesion preparation are limited. Small studies suggest potential benefits of super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons (SH-NCB); however, they have not been directly compared with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL). OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to conduct a randomized comparison of SH-NCBs vs IVL in calcified lesions. METHODS: In this open-label, randomized controlled, noninferiority trial with blinded outcomes assessment (ie, the PROBE design), patients aged ≥18 years with calcified coronary lesions were randomly assigned (1:1) to undergo lesion preparation with SH-NCBs or IVL before PCI with drug-eluting stents. All patients were required to undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT). The primary endpoint was final stent expansion (%) according to OCT. Secondary endpoints included procedural success, strategy success, target vessel failure, stent expansion <80%, and safety outcomes (eg, coronary perforation). RESULTS: Between December 21, 2022, and August 11, 2025, a total of 278 patients underwent the randomly assigned study procedure using plaque modification with SH-NCBs or IVL before stent implantation. The majority of patients (68%) had severe calcium based on an OCT Fujino score ≥4. Study procedures involving IVL tended to be longer and require more auxiliary devices compared with SH-NCBs. The median pressure applied with SH-NCBs compared with IVL was 40 atmospheres vs 6 atmospheres. Regarding the primary endpoint of stent expansion, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL (85% vs 84%; Pnoninferiority < 0.0001). The results were consistent across all subgroups, including calcium severity. Use of SH-NCBs, compared with IVL, resulted in similar rates of procedural and strategy success. Safety outcomes, specifically coronary perforations, did not differ between the 2 groups. At 30 days' follow-up, target vessel failure events (including cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, or myocardial infarction) occurred in 4 (2.8%) patients in the SH-NCB group and in 8 (5.7%) patients in the IVL group (HR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.15 to 1.66; P = 0.26). CONCLUSIONS: In calcified coronary lesions, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL for stent expansion and exhibited a comparable safety profile in experienced operators using intravascular imaging. (Value of IVL Compared To OPN Non-Compliant Balloons for Treatment of Refractory Coronary Lesions [VICTORY]; NCT05346068).

title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
abstract: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.

title: Temporal and Vessel-Specific Relationship Between Post-PCI Fractional Flow Reserve and Long-Term Clinical Outcomes
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) fractional flow reserve (FFR) reflects residual physiological impairment after stent implantation and is a proven predictor of procedural success and prognosis. However, the temporal dynamics of its prognostic utility and its potential variation according to the target vessel remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to explore vessel-specific post-PCI FFR thresholds and evaluate their prognostic consistency over 5 years. METHODS: We analyzed 2128 patients undergoing successful drug-eluting stent implantation from the international Post-PCI FFR Extended registry. Patients were stratified according to the target vessel: left anterior descending artery (LAD) versus non-LAD. The primary end point was 5-year target vessel failure, defined as a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization. Restricted cubic spline models were used to explore the continuous association between post-PCI FFR and target vessel failure and to identify vessel-specific risk thresholds. Temporal prognostic performance was assessed via 3-year landmark analysis and time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic curves. RESULTS: During 5-year follow-up, target vessel failure occurred in 176 patients (11.7%) with LAD lesions and 74 patients (11.7%) with non-LAD lesions.
